Chapter 8: Navigating Setbacks and the Ongoing Nature of Shame.
You know, even after years of working on ourselves, shame has this sneaky way of showing up when we least expect it. Maybe it’s after a bit of criticism, a project that didn’t go as planned, or just an unexpected rejection. Suddenly, those old stories in our heads start whispering again, trying to convince us that nothing’s really changed. It’s so easy in those moments to feel discouraged, isn’t it? You might even catch yourself wondering if all your hard work has really made any difference at all.
Let me share a story with you. There was a woman who’d spent months feeling confident and truly connected. But then, out of the blue, a harsh comment from a family member sent her spiraling. That old familiar wave of inadequacy and self-doubt came rushing right back. For a little while, she slipped into the same old habits: working too much, withdrawing from the people she cared about, even criticizing herself.
But here’s what changed—this time, she noticed what was happening sooner. She reached out to a friend, talked honestly about what she was feeling, and reminded herself that setbacks are just part of the journey.
Most people don’t realize that building resilience to shame isn’t some finish line you cross. It’s an ongoing practice. There will always be moments when something triggers those old wounds. The real difference comes from how quickly you can spot what’s happening—and then choose to respond in a new way.
There’s another story that comes to mind—a woman who’d spent years in therapy and deep self-reflection. Even so, she found herself falling into the old trap of comparing her life to others on social media. That sting of envy and self-judgment? Yeah, it felt just as sharp as ever. But instead of letting herself spiral down, she made a different choice. She logged off, went for a walk, and reminded herself of what truly matters to her—her own values and priorities. The feelings didn’t just vanish, but they lost a lot of their power.
What really stands out here is that setbacks aren’t failures. They’re chances to practice resilience. Every single time you choose self-compassion instead of self-criticism, connection over isolation, honesty instead of silence, you loosen shame’s grip just a little bit more.
The truth is, shame will always be a part of being human. And while that can feel discouraging sometimes, it’s also a reminder that you’re not alone. We all have moments of doubt and struggle. What really matters isn’t avoiding those moments—it’s learning how to move through them, with a little more courage and a lot more grace each time.
